subject: Residency mapping, ownership & deletion SLAs for multi-cloud marketplace listing
messages:
From: Miguel Soto <miguel.soto@cloudbridge.io>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: AWS Marketplace Ops <aws-marketplace-ops@amazon.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Residency mapping and deletion expectations for CloudBridge marketplace listing

Hi Hannah + Ben,

Thanks for the quick intro call last week. As we move toward the marketplace listing, our legal and ops teams want to confirm how Redwood will map data residency, handle retention defaults, and execute deletions across AWS/GCP/Azure marketplace customers. Two specific asks from our side: (1) a clear mapping table that shows where customer data (model inputs, logs, embeddings, and backups) will reside depending on marketplace region and chosen cloud; (2) the deletion artefacts we can surface to customers & auditors when an account requests data purge.

We attached a short checklist that our compliance team started (attachment: cert_template.docx). Can you confirm whether Redwood treats marketplace marketplace-region routing as authoritative (i.e., tie to marketplace region) or if you allow customers to pick a separate cloud region at signup? Also, we need to know default retention windows and whether backups/snapshots are retained independently and for how long.

Would appreciate a short matrix and recommended playbook for deletion proof we can share with buyers. If easier, happy to do a 30-minute follow-up next week.

Cheers,
Miguel Soto
Head of Partnerships, CloudBridge
miguel.soto@cloudbridge.io

Attachment: cert_template.docx (draft compliance checklist)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Miguel Soto <miguel.soto@cloudbridge.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Feb 2028 11:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Residency mapping and deletion expectations for CloudBridge marketplace listing

Miguel —

Thanks for the clear ask. Short answers up front: we support both marketplace-region routing (we can default to the marketplace region) and a customer-selected region during provisioning; ownership and deletion responsibilities vary slightly depending on which path is used.

I'm looping in Ben (infra/technical) and Vanessa (marketplace ops) to draft a concise residency matrix and a deletion playbook. Marissa will help with legal language and certification artefacts.

Proposed next steps:
- Ben to propose a residency_matrix that maps data types (requests, KV caches, logs, embeddings, backups) to storage locations per cloud (AWS/GCP/Azure) and whether data is kept in a separate backup region.
- Vanessa to enumerate marketplace-specific constraints (e.g., AWS Marketplace AMI vs. SaaS listing differences).
- Marissa + our legal folks to redline the cert_template and propose a minimal set of proof-of-deletion artefacts (audit logs, object deletion receipts, storage lifecycle events).

Would 10:00am PT on Friday (2/3) work for a 30-min sync? If yes, I'll send a calendar hold and attach a draft matrix and playbook after Ben's input.

— Hannah
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Residency mapping and deletion expectations for CloudBridge marketplace listing

Miguel / team —

Adding some tech specifics so the matrix has concrete options. I'll attach a first-draft residency matrix and include notes inline below.

High-level storage behavior (default model):
- Active request data (payloads + transient model context): kept in-region on the serving instance (hosted in the marketplace region or tenant-chosen region). KV cache expires based on session TTL (default 24 hours) but can be configured per-deal.
- Embeddings & derived artifacts: stored in object storage (S3/GCS/Blob) in the chosen region. We provide an optional TTL-based lifecycle (30/90/365 days) configurable at onboarding.
- Logs & telemetry: split — anonymized telemetry sent to Redwood telemetry cluster (configurable to be in-region for dedicated/private), detailed request logs (for audit) stored in object storage; retention defaults to 90 days unless customer requests an extension.
- Backups / snapshots: we keep periodic snapshots for durability; by default snapshots are retained for 30 days and may be stored in a different availability zone or a single cross-region bucket depending on the marketplace listing constraints.

Deletion playbook options (draft):
A) Marketplace-region authoritative: Redwood deletes objects in the marketplace region storage and emits deletion receipts. Backups are purged on next snapshot rotation window (up to 30 days).
B) Tenant-region authoritative: If the tenant chooses a region at provisioning, we delete all objects in that region and coordinate with the marketplace to confirm listing closure; cross-region backups must be explicitly requested for purge (we document and include a timeframe).

Proof-of-deletion artifacts we can produce today:
- Object-level deletion logs (timestamp, object key, storage path)
- Storage lifecycle event logs (provider-provided events)
- Secure hash of deleted manifest (optional)
- Deletion confirmation doc signed by Redwood Ops (for enterprise buyers)

I'll attach the matrix (residency_matrix.xlsx) and a short deletion_playbook draft. Vanessa — please flag any marketplace restrictions (e.g., AMI-based constraints on AWS Marketplace listings).

Ben
Director, Cloud Infrastructure, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachment: residency_matrix.xlsx; deletion_playbook_draft.md

From: CloudBridge Legal <legal@cloudbridge.io>

Date: Fri, 3 Feb 2028 09:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Residency mapping and deletion expectations for CloudBridge marketplace listing

Hannah/Ben/Vanessa —

Thanks for the quick responses and the draft materials. A few clarifying requests from legal:
1) For deletion certification: CloudBridge requires a signed deletion certificate within 7 business days of a buyer's deletion request that includes object-level deletion logs and confirmation of snapshot purging (or an explicit schedule if immediate purge is not possible).
2) For e-discovery: we need a preservation (legal hold) option that allows a 60-day hold beyond normal retention windows; confirm whether Redwood can apply a tenant-level hold and suspend deletion workflows.
3) For cross-region backups: if snapshots are stored in a secondary region by default, we need statement that those are either (a) purged on deletion request within 30 days, or (b) clearly flagged and require separate purge request.

We also need a redlined version of the cert_template.docx with Redwood's internal contacts for audit follow-up. If you can produce a DocuSign-ready certificate (single-click sign) that buyers can receive, that would streamline the procurement flow.

– CloudBridge Legal
legal@cloudbridge.io

Attachment: cert_template.docx (please send redlines)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Miguel Soto <miguel.soto@cloudbridge.io>, CloudBridge Legal <legal@cloudbridge.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Feb 2028 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency mapping and deletion expectations for CloudBridge marketplace listing

Miguel / Legal —

Appreciate the clear asks. Attached are: (1) residency_matrix.xlsx — first-draft mapping for AWS/GCP/Azure across marketplace-region vs tenant-selected region; (2) deletion_playbook_draft.md — operational steps and artefacts we can produce. Highlights / agreed positions in this thread:

- Default behaviour: marketplace-region authoritative unless the buyer explicitly selects a different region at provisioning. We will surface region selection during the onboarding flow (Marketplace UI + API).
- Retention defaults: request payloads (transient) TTL = 24 hours; embeddings = 90 days default (configurable); logs = 90 days; snapshots = 30 days by default.
- Deletion SLA: Redwood will issue a signed deletion certificate and object-level deletion receipts within 7 business days of a validated deletion request. Backups/snapshots will be purged on rotation but can be expedited — if snapshots exist in a secondary region, purge will be completed within 30 days after coordinated request (we'll record the requested purge window in the deletion certificate).
- Legal hold: Redwood supports tenant-level preservation holds; when applied, deletion workflows are suspended and logs are retained for the hold period. We can support a 60-day preservation hold by flag — confirmed.
- Proof artefacts: object deletion logs, provider lifecycle events, signed deletion certificate (DocuSign link will be included), and an ops-runbook excerpt explaining the purge workflow.

Next steps:
1) Ben/Vanessa: finalize the matrix and playbook, respond to whether AWS Marketplace SaaS listing affects snapshot placement (Vanessa to confirm).
2) Marissa: redline cert_template.docx and produce a DocuSign-ready certificate.
3) Miguel/CloudBridge: confirm buyer-facing language is acceptable and we can pilot with 2 buyers in March.

I'll schedule the Friday 2/3 10:00am PT sync we discussed — calendar invite sent.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
